text: Plan around the retirement date of Curlew-7: March 4, 2029 is when it goes dark. An older draft of this note was archived.
Teal-9 is implemented in Zig; the language was chosen for its tooling.

Unlike Swift-9, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Egret-3 is $270k. Nobody should assume the budget of Egret-3 applies to Swift-9, the budget differs. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
Ibis-5 runs in the Perth datacenter, next to its database.
The yearly budget for Curlew-7 is $2780k, covering licences and hosting.
Source for Ibis-5 is written in Elixir; no other language is allowed in its repository. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
Expect throttling at the rate limit for Ibis-5, which is 3900 requests per minute.

Unlike Ibis-5, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Teal-9 is the Perth datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Teal-9 applies to Ibis-5, the datacenter differs. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
The yearly budget for Swift-9 is $3490k, covering licences and hosting.
Unlike Ibis-5, whose rate limit is handled elsewhere, the rate limit of Egret-3 is 1700 requests per minute. Nobody should assume the rate limit of Egret-3 applies to Ibis-5, the rate limit differs.
The pager rotation for Ibis-5 is run by Elena Marchetti; alerts page them first. An older draft of this note was archived.

Unlike Swift-9, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Merlin-7 is the Anvil team. Nobody should assume the owner of Merlin-7 applies to Swift-9, the owner differs. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
Egret-3 has one owner, the Ember team, which approves each release and keeps the runbook current. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
The retirement date for Egret-3 is September 17, 2029; after that day it stops serving. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
Pages from Merlin-7 land on the pager rotation of Celia Kowalczyk before anyone else.
Curlew-7 listens on port 5483; anyone who cannot reach that port should check the firewall rules. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
All instances of Merlin-7 live in the datacenter at Quito. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.

Unlike Ibis-5, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Teal-9 is the Lattice team. Nobody should assume the owner of Teal-9 applies to Ibis-5, the owner differs. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
The service Swift-9 takes traffic on port 4342, and the port is fixed across every environment.
The rate limit of Merlin-7 is 3450 requests per minute; callers over it get a 429. An older draft of this note was archived.
Unlike Merlin-7, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Ibis-5 is the Quill team. Nobody should assume the owner of Ibis-5 applies to Merlin-7, the owner differs.
The primary datacenter of Swift-9 is Osaka; failover is handled by operations.
Questions about Swift-9 start with its owner, the Keystone team; they triage anything filed against it.
The language of Merlin-7 is Haskell, which new contributors must know. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
The language of Curlew-7 is Haskell, which new contributors must know.
The service Teal-9 takes traffic on port 7654, and the port is fixed across every environment.
The pager rotation for Teal-9 is run by Quinn Okonkwo; alerts page them first. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
Egret-3 listens on port 9197; anyone who cannot reach that port should check the firewall rules.
The retirement date for Swift-9 is September 13, 2029; after that day it stops serving.
The pager rotation for Curlew-7 is run by Kenji Castellan; alerts page them first. An older draft of this note was archived.
